content: 1. Ebadi et al. conducted a randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial to evaluate the effects of continuous ultrasound therapy on patients suffering from low back pain. The study was published in Electromyography and Clinical Neurophysiology in 2006. 2. Durmuş et al. investigated the therapeutic effects of ultrasound on pain, disability, walking performance, quality of life, and depression in patients with chronic low back pain. This randomized, placebo-controlled trial was published in Archives of Rheumatology in 2010. 3. Durmuş, Durmaz, and Canturk examined the combined effects of therapeutic ultrasound and electrical stimulation on pain, trunk muscle strength, disability, walking performance, quality of life, and depression in patients with low back pain. Their findings were published in Rheumatology International in 2010. 4. Durmuş et al. explored the efficacy of phonophoresis in treating chronic low back pain through a single-blind, randomized controlled trial. The results were published in Rheumatology International in 2013. 5. Ebadi et al. assessed the impact of continuous ultrasound therapy on chronic non-specific low back pain in a single-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial. The study was published in BMC Musculoskeletal Disorders in 2012. 6. Grubišić et al. evaluated the role of therapeutic ultrasound in the treatment of chronic low back pain. Their findings were published in Reumatizam in 2006. 7. Khan et al. compared the effects of combined ultrasound and exercise therapy versus exercise therapy alone in managing chronic back pain. The study was published in the Indian Journal of Physiotherapy and Occupational Therapy in 2013. 8. Licciardone et al. conducted a randomized controlled trial to compare osteopathic manual treatment and ultrasound therapy for chronic low back pain. The results were published in Annals of Family Medicine in 2013. 9. Rubira et al. compared the effects of low-level laser therapy, pulsed ultrasound, and continuous ultrasound on pain and physical disability in patients with chronic non-specific low back pain. The study was published in Advances in Rheumatology in 2019. 10. Tantawy et al. demonstrated that laser photobiomodulation is more effective than ultrasound therapy in treating chronic non-specific low back pain. Their comparative study was published in Lasers in Medical Science in 2019. 11. Tanveer et al. investigated the effects of low-intensity pulsed ultrasound on pain and functional disability in patients with early-stage lumbar spondylolysis. The randomized controlled trial was published in the Journal of Bodywork and Movement Therapies in 2022. 12. Yurdakul et al. studied the effects of physical therapy modalities on pain, disability, quality of life, and lumbar paravertebral muscle stiffness using elastography in patients with chronic low back pain. The findings were published in the Turkish Journal of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation in 2019. 13. Shimoji et al. evaluated the analgesic effects of transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS) using bidirectional modulated sine waves in patients with chronic back pain. The randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled study was published in Neuromodulation in 2007. 14. Alizadeh and Ahmadizad compared the efficacy of exercise therapy and TENS in treating chronic low back pain. Their findings were published in the World Journal of Sport Sciences in 2009. 15. Bloodworth et al. compared stochastic versus conventional TENS for pain modulation in patients with electromyographically documented radiculopathy. The study was published in the American Journal of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation in 2004. 16. The World Health Organization (WHO) released guidelines for the non-surgical management of chronic primary low back pain in adults within primary and community care settings. 17. Cheing and Hui-Chan explored the non-parallel antinociceptive effects of TENS on chronic clinical pain and acute experimental pain. Their study was published in Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation in 1999. 18. De Alencar Caldas et al. assessed the effects of pain education, cryotherapy, and TENS on pain, functional capacity, and quality of life in patients with non-specific chronic low back pain. The single-blind randomized controlled trial was published in the American Journal of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation in 2021. 19. Depaoli Lemos et al. compared electroacupuncture and TENS in managing chronic non-specific low back pain. The blind randomized clinical trial was published in the Muscles, Ligaments, and Tendons Journal in 2021. 20. Dias et al. evaluated the immediate analgesic effects of TENS and interferential current (IFC) on chronic low back pain in a randomized placebo-controlled trial. The study was published in the Journal of Bodywork and Movement Therapies in 2021. 21. Elserty et al. compared fixed versus adjusted TENS amplitude in treating chronic mechanical low back pain. The findings were published in the Journal of Alternative and Complementary Medicine in 2016. 22. Ezema et al. investigated the effects of TENS on pain intensity and endogenous opioid levels in patients with chronic low back pain. The randomized controlled trial was published in the Journal of Back and Musculoskeletal Rehabilitation in 2022. 23. Jamison et al. evaluated the outcomes of a high-frequency TENS device for low back pain in a randomized controlled trial. The study was published in Pain Practice in 2019. 24. Kibar et al. assessed the combined efficacy of TENS and interferential current therapy in managing chronic low back pain. The randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled study was published in the Turkish Journal of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation in 2020. 25. Koftolis et al. conducted a sequentially allocated clinical trial to evaluate rhythmic stabilization exercises and TENS in women with chronic low back pain. The study was published in Clinical Rehabilitation in 2008. 26. Petrofsky et al. examined the effects of TENS and low-level continuous heat on non-specific low back pain in a randomized controlled trial. The findings were published in Gazzetta Medica Italiana in 2020. 27. Tella et al. evaluated the efficacy of TENS and interferential current on tactile acuity in individuals with non-specific chronic low back pain. The study was published in Neuromodulation in 2022. 28. Topuz et al. compared the efficacy of TENS and percutaneous neuromodulation therapy in treating chronic low back pain. The findings were published in the Journal of Back and Musculoskeletal Rehabilitation in 2004. 29. Yaksi et al. investigated the effects of TENS on pain, neuropathic pain, and sympathetic skin responses in chronic low back pain treatment. The randomized, placebo-controlled study was published in the Korean Journal of Pain in 2021. 30. Annaswamy et al. conducted a randomized controlled trial to evaluate lumbar bracing for chronic low back pain. The study was published in the American Journal of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation in 2021. 31. Ay Uslusoy and Savas compared the effectiveness of extension-controlled lumbar support and elastic lumbar support in managing chronic low back pain in a short-term follow-up. The study was published in the Turkish Journal of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation in 2013. 32. Azadinia et al. conducted a randomized controlled trial comparing lumbosacral orthosis to routine physical therapy for postural stability in patients with chronic low back pain. The study was published in the Medical Journal of the Islamic Republic of Iran in 2017. 33. Dalichau and Scheele evaluated the effects of elastic lumbar belts on the outcomes of a muscle training program for patients with chronic back pain. The study was published in Z Orthop Ihre Grenzgeb in 2000. 34. Samani et al. compared the long-term use of soft lumbosacral orthoses at two different pressures in patients with chronic non-specific low back pain. The randomized controlled trial was published in Clinical Biomechanics in 2019. 35. Sato et al. investigated the effects of long-term corset wearing on chronic low back pain. The study was published in Fukushima Journal of Medical Science in 2012. 36. Shakoor et al. evaluated the effects of lumbosacral corsets on patients with chronic non-specific low back pain. The study was published in the Indian Journal of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation in 2015. 37. Aliyu et al. assessed the effects of combined lumbar stabilization exercises and cognitive behavioral therapy on selected variables in individuals with non-specific low back pain. The randomized clinical trial was published in Fisioterapia in 2018. 38. Altmaier et al. evaluated the effectiveness of psychological interventions for the rehabilitation of low back pain in a randomized controlled trial. The study was published in Pain in 1992. 39. Banth and Ardebil examined the effectiveness of mindfulness meditation on pain and quality of life in patients with chronic low back pain. The study was published in the International Journal of Yoga in 2015. 40. Basler et al. incorporated cognitive-behavioral treatment into the medical care of chronic low back pain patients in a controlled randomized study conducted in German pain treatment centers. The study was published in Patient Education and Counseling in 1997. 41. Baumeister et al. evaluated the effectiveness of a guided internetand mobile-based intervention for patients with chronic back pain and depression in a multicenter, pragmatic randomized controlled trial. The study was published in Psychotherapy and Psychosomatics in 2021. 42. Buhrman et al. demonstrated that guided internet-based cognitive behavioral treatment reduces pain catastrophizing in patients with chronic back pain. The randomized controlled trial was published in the Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine in 2011. 43. Bush et al. conducted a controlled evaluation of paraspinal EMG biofeedback in the treatment of chronic low back pain. The study was published in Health Psychology in 1985. 44. Carpenter et al. assessed the efficacy of an online self-help CBT intervention for chronic lower back pain. The study was published in the Clinical Journal of Pain in 2012. 45. Cherkin et al. compared mindfulness-based stress reduction, cognitive behavioral therapy, and usual care for back pain and functional limitations in adults with chronic low back pain. The randomized clinical trial was published in JAMA in 2016. 46. Christiansen et al. evaluated a short goal-pursuit intervention to improve physical capacity in chronic back pain patients. The randomized clinical trial was published in Pain in 2010. 47. Friedrich et al. assessed the long-term effects of a combined exercise and motivational program on the level of disability in patients with chronic low back pain. The study was published in Spine in 2005. 48. Glombiewski et al. demonstrated the effectiveness of two psychological interventions in severely disabled chronic back pain patients in a randomized controlled trial. The study was published in the International Journal of Behavioral Medicine in 2010. 49. Goossens et al. conducted a health economic assessment of behavioral rehabilitation in chronic low back pain through a randomized clinical trial. The study was published in Health Economics in 1998. 50. Johnson et al. evaluated the effects of active exercise, education, and cognitive behavioral therapy on persistent disabling low back pain in a randomized controlled trial. The study was published in Spine in 2007. 51. Kapitza et al. compared non-contingent respiratory biofeedback placebo versus contingent biofeedback in patients with chronic low back pain in a randomized, controlled, double-blind trial. The study was published in Applied Psychophysiology and Biofeedback in 2010. 52. Khan et al. assessed the effectiveness of cognitive behavioral therapy combined with general exercises versus general exercises alone in managing chronic low back pain.
